methods.label: Check the theorem's conditions
methods.explanation: A corollary of the perpendicular diameter theorem states that a diameter bisecting a chord (that is not a diameter) is perpendicular to the chord and bisects the arcs subtended by the chord. If the chord itself is a diameter, any two diameters bisect each other but are not necessarily perpendicular. A line perpendicular to a chord does not necessarily pass through the center.
